doc.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Coltrane's changing direction in the mid-1960s
summary: Brower asks whether people debated where Coltrane was going; Walton says not then, praises Elvin and McCoy as perfect fits, and admits he was focused on his own career with Blakey.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Was there, was there a … I know that there was a, people were – and I don't want to be stuck on Trane, since we're here … um … Trane uh … What was the uh, the band was really
opening, I mean, by the mid-Sixties, the band was really like getting' open and Trane and Elvin were like goin' in this direction …

… of how, how people were sort of astounded, amazed by his work ethic and you know, definitely appreciated him as someone who had gone through all the stages … no one could question, Was he grounded in the tradition or not.
Was there starting to be some uh, debate or discussion about where he was takin' the music?

Uh, no. Not at that moment when we played opposite each other. He would play uh, uh, uh … let's see, what's that song uh, My Favorite Things and uh Naima and uh, uh, his uh, his Bebop sort of like uh …
Yeah, yeah, definitely, yeah. It was just uh, what Elvin adding a definite new flavor. Elvin's playing was totally original in my view. And uh, a total fit for uh, for Coltrane, John Coltrane.
What about where McCoy was going?
Yeah, yeah, same thing, a perfect fit. It was a … they were making history.
Could you at that time have any sense of where he would go with this music?

No. No, we were thinkin' about ourselves, man. I mean, it's a good question, mind you, had I been an historian, but I was workin' with … where can I see the Walton's career with Art Blakey then. So I was enjoyin', just enjoyin' the music just like any other fan. What direction they were goin' in didn't, just didn't occur to me, like it would perhaps to you. But not to me. But uh, uh, I think it's a very valid question but uh, I'm just not prepared to give you much input in it because I can remember that I was so delighted to be in this group that I was in, you know. And such a, uh, first-rate group, you know, to be in the Messengers.
